newsitem.title: INDIA: India's PM told to seek confidence vote by April 7.
newsitem.headline: India's PM told to seek confidence vote by April 7.

text.p: India's Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda has been asked to seek a vote of confidence in the Lok Sabha, the lower house of parliament, by Monday April 7, a spokesman in President Shankar Dayal Sharma's office told Reuters on Monday.
"The President has requested the Prime Minister to seek a vote of confidence in the Lok Sabha by Monday April 7," the spokesman quoted a presidential communique as saying.

Sharma's directive ended speculation about whether parliament would meet on April 21 as scheduled to resume discusion on the budget for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) or be summoned earlier to enable the prime minister to face the trust vote.
Deve Gowda said earlier on Monday he would face parliament next month and was not planning to resign after the Congress party withdrew its make-or-break support for his 10-month old government.
A Congress official told Reuters his party had formally staked its claim before Sharma on Monday to head a new government.
The Congress withdrew its support for the ruling United Front alliance on Sunday, accusing Deve Gowda of failing to counter check the growth of communalism among other reasons.
